title: Evaluating Novel Approaches for Estimating Awake and Sleep Blood Pressure
brief_summary: The purpose of the proposed study is to test whether measuring unattended blood pressure using an automated blood pressure monitor in a clinic setting without staff being present can reduce the need for assessing out-of- clinic awake blood pressure using ambulatory monitoring. Also, the investigators will test whether asleep blood pressure can be accurately measured using a novel home blood pressure monitoring device with less burden compared with ambulatory monitoring.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Mean screening systolic blood pressure of 110 to \< 160 mm Hg at most recent visit
* Mean screening diastolic blood pressure of 70 to \<100 mm Hg at most recent visit

Exclusion Criteria:

* Currently taking antihypertensive medications
* Known to be currently pregnant
* History of sleep apnea
* History of heart attack, stroke, or any cardiovascular disease
* History of arrhythmia (e.g. - atrial fibrillation or ventricular tachycardia)
* Completed ambulatory blood pressure monitoring in the past year
* Second shift, overnight, or jobs that will not allow ambulatory blood pressure device to measure every 30 minutes for 24 hours.
